clue.text: Pays for seats

definitions.meaning: to pay a bill is to clear or square it
wooden benches with high backs are a kind of seat

explanation.definitionFit: To settle an account is to pay it off, and a settle is a long high-backed wooden bench, so the plural names seats.

clue.text: Corner man in the House?

parts.note: the man of a famous corner in Hyde Park is an orator, and the chair of the House of Commons bears the same title

explanation.walkthrough: Corner man suggests a boxer's second, but it points to Speakers' Corner in Hyde Park, London, and the presiding officer of the House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone orating at Hyde Park's corner holds this title, as does the Commons chair.

clue.text: Standard French description of many others

definitions.meaning: the national flag of France, its blue, white and red standard
a word for any flag of three colours, true of many national flags

explanation.definitionFit: The French flag has three bands, and the word describes any such three-coloured banner, as in Italy or Ireland.

clue.text: Like old yeomen and lieges, original characters

definitions.text: Like old yeomen and lieges, original characters

indicators.note: original characters are the opening letters of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Faithful followers of old are described as true originals.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of 'Like old yeomen and lieges' spell the answer, and the whole clue defines it too.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieges and yeomen of old were bound to faithful service, the quality of staying true.

clue.text: Plant from deep South coming up with source of oil

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
an oil well is where oil comes from

explanation.surface: A plant grows in the Deep South beside an oil field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns DEEPS into SPEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell is a small wild flower, usually blue, of the genus Veronica.

clue.text: Lamb after highball in the plant

parts.note: a lob is a ball hit or thrown high
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: Someone finds lamb on the menu after a cocktail in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts ELIA behind LOB. 'Lamb' and 'highball' suggest food and drink, but one is the essayist and the other a high-hit ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a garden flowering plant, often grown in blue edging and hanging baskets.

clue.text: Put up at the cottage

definitions.meaning: to stay as a guest or give someone a room
a small house, such as a gatekeeper's at an estate entrance

explanation.definitionFit: To lodge is to stay overnight somewhere, and a lodge is a small house at the gates of an estate.

clue.text: A way for wets to be right maybe

definitions.text: A way for wets to be right maybe

parts.words: A way for wets to be right maybe
parts.note: wets were moderate Tories, the Bow Group is a Conservative circle, and a street is a way

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wets' were moderate Conservatives under Thatcher; the Bow Group is a Tory think-tank, so a street named Bow might lead them right. Bow Street is a London street, home of the Runners and a famous court.
explanation.definitionFit: Bow Street is a London road, and the Bow Group gives moderate Tories a route to the political right.

clue.text: Knowing shelter on the line

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
RY, railway, stands for a line

explanation.surface: Someone shrewd takes cover by the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A leery person is wary and wise to tricks, so knowing.

clue.text: Choral items, include them in a brief reply

indicators.note: include means the shortened reply goes round the other word

parts.note: ANS is the short form of answer, a reply
taken as written

explanation.surface: Choir pieces should be mentioned in a short response.
explanation.walkthrough: 'include' puts THEM inside ANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthems are choral compositions, often sung in church services.

clue.text: Keeper's keeper so called at the parsonage

definitions.text: Keeper's keeper so called at the parsonage

parts.words: Keeper's keeper so called at the parsonage
parts.note: Keeper was the dog owned by one of the Bronte sisters at Haworth parsonage; we want the first name of its owner

explanation.walkthrough: Keeper sounds like a goalkeeper or zookeeper, but it was the dog of Emily Bronte, who lived at the parsonage at Haworth in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist Bronte, author of Wuthering Heights, owned the mastiff Keeper and lived at her father's parsonage.

clue.text: Women tend to be troubled by this policy?

indicators.note: letters that are troubled are disturbed and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain insurance plan worries women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be troubled' shuffles WOMEN and TEND together.
explanation.definitionFit: An endowment is a type of life-insurance policy that pays out a lump sum at the end of a fixed term.

clue.text: Jowett knew it all

parts.note: the Balliol rhyme has the Master Benjamin Jowett saying that what he does not know is not worth calling learning, so all of it was in his head

explanation.walkthrough: A rhyme of Oxford's Balliol College has its Master, Benjamin Jowett, say: 'What I don't know isn't knowledge'.
explanation.definitionFit: If Jowett knew everything, then the whole store of learning is what he possessed.

clue.text: Herb's the enemy, they say

indicators.note: they say means the word is spoken and we hear its sound

parts.note: 'time, the enemy' is a set phrase: time is the foe that ages us

explanation.surface: Someone declares a certain herb to be a foe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb's' stands for 'herb is', so the definition is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is an aromatic culinary herb of the mint family.

clue.text: Settle for sleep in a kangaroo stockyard

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the run of the words kangaroo stockyard

explanation.surface: An animal beds down for the night in an Australian pen.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across kangaROO STockyard.
explanation.definitionFit: To roost is to perch or settle down to sleep, as birds do at night.

clue.text: Tablet in the cup is insipid

indicators.note: in shows the slab sits inside the cup

parts.note: a tass is a small cup or goblet, a Scots word
a stele is an upright inscribed stone slab or tablet

explanation.surface: A pill dissolved in a drink makes it bland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tablet' suggests medicine, but it is a carved stone slab, STELE, set into TASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tasteless has no flavour, which is what insipid means.

clue.text: Note runes may be deciphered confidentially

indicators.note: deciphering a code sorts its letters into a new readable order

explanation.surface: Ancient runic writing can be read in secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be deciphered' rearranges NOTE and RUNES.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means 'between ourselves', said of something told in confidence.

clue.text: Will teams change under canvas?

indicators.note: under canvas puts the shuffled letters inside the tent

parts.note: a tent is made of canvas, so to be under canvas is to be in one

indicators.note: change means the letters of teams are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question whether sports teams will swap players while camping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges TEAMS to STAME, and 'under' puts it inside TENT. 'Will' looks like a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will and testament is the legal document leaving a person's estate.

clue.text: Terribly squalid in an Old Etonian to be a slave

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the abbreviation

parts.note: OE is the abbreviation for an Old Etonian, a former pupil of Eton College

indicators.note: terribly signals the word squalid is mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A slave finds conditions dreadful in the home of a privileged former schoolboy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' rearranges SQUALID to DALISQU, and 'in' puts it inside OE.
explanation.definitionFit: An odalisque was a female slave or concubine in an Ottoman harem.

clue.text: What a pup, or Alice's hookah-smoker, would turn into?

definitions.text: What a pup, or Alice's hookah-smoker, would turn into?

parts.words: What a pup, or Alice's hookah-smoker, would turn into?
parts.note: the hookah-smoker in Alice in Wonderland is the Caterpillar, and 'pup' hints at the pupa stage a caterpillar forms

explanation.walkthrough: A pup suggests a young dog, but read it as the start of pupa; the hookah-smoking Caterpillar of Lewis Carroll's story would become a pupa too.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterpillar enters the pupal stage inside a hard case before emerging as a butterfly.

clue.text: Many a girl in the city

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
Hester is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Lots of young women live in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the' is a link: the girl HESTER follows C.
explanation.definitionFit: Chester is a walled cathedral city in Cheshire, England.

clue.text: Track events in IOM with no start or finish

indicators.note: no start or finish means the first and last letters of the phrase are dropped

parts.note: the TT races are the motorcycle events held on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Motorcycle racing on the Isle of Man runs without a start line or chequered flag.
explanation.walkthrough: IOM is the Isle of Man, home of the TT motorcycle races; dropping the first and last letters of TT RACES leaves the answer. 'Track' looks like part of the racing scene but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace someone is to follow or track them down.

clue.text: Beg quarters and free entertainment

parts.note: E and N, east and north, are compass quarters
a treat is something given for nothing to entertain

explanation.surface: Someone pleads for lodgings and a free show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' suggests lodgings, but it means two points of the compass.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to plead earnestly, to beg.

clue.text: Little man makes one German soldier retreat

indicators.note: retreat means go backwards, so the letters are read the other way

parts.note: ein is German for one
RE, Royal Engineers, stands for a soldier

explanation.surface: A small man makes a German soldier withdraw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' turns EINRE round. Ernie Wise, the short half of the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise, was the 'little man' of the act.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie Wise was the shorter partner whom Eric Morecambe teased as the one with short, fat, hairy legs.

clue.text: Half-point return here in France

indicators.note: return means coming back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: semi is a prefix meaning half
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A traveller makes a brief round trip somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns SEMIN round.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimes is a city in southern France, known for its Roman arena.

clue.text: Playwright takes tot with painter right away

parts.note: a tot is a small drink of spirits, a dram

indicators.note: away tells us to take the letter out

parts.note: a painter is an artist

explanation.surface: A writer of plays has a nip of whisky with an artist friend at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately' but means remove R, leaving ATIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatist writes plays for the stage, so is a playwright.

clue.text: Mr Acheson's chapter heads

definitions.meaning: belonging to Dean Acheson, the US Secretary of State
the heads of a cathedral's governing chapter

explanation.definitionFit: Dean Acheson's first name with a possessive gives the word, and cathedral chapters are led by deans.

clue.text: Law alternatively is one concerned with part performance

parts.note: an act is a law passed by Parliament
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Legislation is offered as an option for someone who plays roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part performance' sounds like a legal term, but it means playing a part.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor performs a role in a play or film.

clue.text: Consumed with anger, yet self-restrained

parts.note: temper is a fit of anger
ate means consumed, as food

explanation.surface: Someone eaten up by rage still manages to keep control.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperate describes moderation and self-control, avoiding excess.

clue.text: Headgear connected to what French fashion?

parts.note: que is French for what

explanation.surface: A question about which hat goes with the latest French style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'connected' just joins TO to QUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A toque is a small brimless hat, also the tall white hat of a chef.

clue.text: Opposes one in stress perhaps

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the shuffled word
perhaps shows the word stress is only one possible order of these letters

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A person pushes back against pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges STRESS to RESSTS, and 'in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist something is to stand against or fight it.

clue.text: It rushes down from rocky height, torn

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor
rent means torn, as of cloth

explanation.surface: A stream crashes down from a craggy summit, tearing its way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' just joins the definition to the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a fast, violent stream of water pouring downhill.
